tests.procedure: Under strong white light, check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and compliance with the visual specification.

details.vessel: clean, transparent watch glass or glass dish

tests.procedure: To 10 mL of water add [amount unreadable: 'add 0 ml of sample']; the sample is miscible with water.

To 25 mL of sample add 50 mL of water and 35 mL of hydrogen peroxide solution (20 vol). Titrate with 0.5 M hydrochloric acid VS using methyl orange solution as indicator. Determine the weight per mL of the solution. Calculate total alkalinity as % w/w, as NaOH.

details.equivalenceFactor: Each mL of 0.5 M hydrochloric acid VS is equivalent to 20 mg of NaOH
details.weightPerMl: Determine the weight per mL of the solution (procedure not stated)

formulaTerms.Wt: weight of sample equivalent to weight per mL
formulaTerms.20: equivalent of NaOH (mg per mL titrant)

details.titrantPreparation: 0.5 M HCl VS: dilute 51.5 g of hydrochloric acid to 1000.0 mL with water
details.titrantStandardization: Dissolve 0.950 g Tris in 50 mL water; titrate with the HCl solution, endpoint potentiometric; 1 mL of 1 M HCl is equivalent to 121.1 mg Tris
details.indicatorPreparation: Methyl orange solution: dissolve 0.1 g methyl orange in 80 mL water and dilute to 100 mL with ethanol (96 per cent)

tests.source: Sodium Hypochlorite__STM Sodium Hypochlorite.txt:32; preparations line 28

tests.procedure: Dilute 10 mL to 250 mL with water. Add 10 mL of the resulting solution to a mixture of 50 mL water, 1 g potassium iodide and 12.5 mL of 2 M acetic acid. Titrate with 0.1 M sodium thiosulfate VS using starch solution as indicator. Determine the weight per mL of the solution. Calculate % w/w available chlorine.

details.aliquotAddedTo: 50 mL water + 1 g potassium iodide + 12.5 mL of 2 M acetic acid
details.equivalenceFactor: Each mL of 0.1 M sodium thiosulfate VS is equivalent to 3.545 mg of Cl
details.weightPerMl: Determine the weight per mL of the solution (procedure not stated)
details.formula: % W/W of Chlorine = (EP x Eq.w x F) / Wt x 100

formulaTerms.Wt: weight of sample equivalent to weight per mL

details.titrantPreparation: 0.1 M sodium thiosulfate VS: dissolve 25 g sodium thiosulfate and 0.2 g sodium carbonate in carbon dioxide-free water, dilute to 1000.0 mL with the same solvent
details.titrantStandardization: To 10.0 mL of 0.033 M potassium bromate add 40 mL water, 10 mL potassium iodide solution R and 5 mL hydrochloric acid R1; titrate with the thiosulfate solution, starch solution (1 mL) added towards the end as indicator; 1 mL of 0.1 M sodium thiosulfate is equivalent to 2.783 mg of potassium bromate or 0.5 mL of 0.033 M potassium bromate

standardPreparations.0.033 M potassium bromate VS: dissolve 5.5670 g potassium bromate in water, dilute to 1000.0 mL
standardPreparations.hydrochloric acid R1: dilute 70 g hydrochloric acid to 100 mL with water
standardPreparations.potassium iodide solution: dissolve 16.6 g potassium iodide in water, complete to 100 mL
standardPreparations.starch solution: triturate 1.0 g soluble starch with 5 mL water, pour with stirring into 100 mL boiling water containing 10 mg mercuric iodide
standardPreparations.carbon dioxide-free water: water boiled a few minutes and protected from the atmosphere during cooling and storage

openQuestions.question: Miscibility procedure reads 'To 10 ml of water add 0 ml of sample': the sample volume is 0 mL, which is not a usable amount. What volume of sample is added?

Assay formula '(EP x Eq.w x F) / Wt x 100' has no dilution factor (10 mL diluted to 250 mL, 10 mL aliquot) and no mg-to-g conversion, unlike the Total alkalinity formula which has /1000. Confirm the intended calculation.

'Weight per mL of the solution' / 'Wt: weight of sample equivalent to weight per ml' is used in both formulas but the procedure to determine it (density method, sample volume) is not stated. For total alkalinity, is Wt the weight of the 25 mL taken? For assay, of the 10 mL taken?
Preparation of '2 M acetic acid' and 'hydrogen peroxide solution (20 vol)' is not given in the STM reagent list.
The 0.5 M HCl standardization quotes the factor for 1 M HCl (1 mL of 1 M HCl = 121.1 mg Tris); the factor for 0.5 M HCl is not stated, and the Tris amount (0.950 g) is the only quantity given.
Spec reference for the assay says '% of chlorine' while STM says % w/w available chlorine; w/w and as-is basis inferred, confirm.
